definition: The SI unit of temperature, symbol K, with no degree sign. The kelvin scale starts at absolute zero ($0\ \text{K}$), and a change of 1 K is the same as a change of 1 °C, so $T$ (in K) $= \theta$ (in °C) $+ 273$.

For a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, pressure × volume stays the same: $pV = \text{constant}$. Halving the volume doubles the pressure, and a graph of $p$ against $\frac{1}{V}$ is a straight line through the origin.
